newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia stocks close higher, Philippine shares rally.
newsitem.headline: Asia stocks close higher, Philippine shares rally.

text.p: Most Asian markets closed higher on Monday, propelled by Friday's gains on Wall Street, with the most dramatic gains seen in Hong Kong and Manila.
Philippine stocks, which have been battered in recent weeks amid fears of a real estate melt-down and weak corporate earnings, rallied, although analysts questioned the strength of the recovery.
Tokyo markets were closed for a holiday, but Hong Kong was open and traders sent the Hang Seng Index surging in a follow- through to New York's gains.
The market ended 317.64 points, or 2.43 percent, higher at 13,399.34.
"Wall Street was strong and there is some switching out of red chips Into property and banking (stocks) and that is why the index is up," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Wall Street's strength on Friday followed the release of positive economic data and an agreement to balance the budget, fuelling a 94.72-point rise in the Dow Jones Industrial Average to 7,071.20.

Although the economic data revealed signs of a tight labour market -- the unemployment rate dropped to 4.9 percent -- traders were heartened by a smaller-than-expected rise of 142,000 in non-farm payrolls.
The data, however, did not quash the debate among economists over whether the Federal Reserve will push interest rates up when policy makers meet again on May 20.
A Reuters poll in New York showed 22 of 29 economists expected the Fed to hike rates another quarter of a percentage point at the meeting.

In the Philippines, a burst of bargain-hunting sparked a rise of more than five percent in the main stock index, but dealers stopped short of saying the worst was over for the recently troubled market.
The exchange opened higher and continued to advance, eventually gaining 130.77 points, or 5.02 percent, to close at the day's high of 2,736.42.

"We did not expect a technical rebound this big, but I say that this has to be sustained for at least a week before we can say with conviction that there has been a reversal," said Helen Alvarex, research director at All Asia Securities.

The buying spree lifted shares of Megaworld Properties and Holdings Inc and its housing arm Empire East Land Hondings Inc, which had been badly hurt in recent weeks by fears of an oversupply in the property sector.
In Indonesia the Jakarta composite index was up a modest 4.89 points, or 0.76 percent, at 652.787 in quiet trading.

A report was released on Sunday in Canada stating that the Busang gold discovery on Borneo island, touted as one of the biggest finds ever, had been falsified. But the report had only a moderate impact on the market, dealers said.
Mining company Tambang Timah fell 125 rupiah to 3,800 rupiah in light volume, even though the company did not have any involvement in the project.
Brokers in Australia predicted a mild negative effect on the Australian gold sector following the Busang reports.
Australian stocks lost their early enthusiasm and ended only 1.1 points, or 0.04 percent, higher at 2,492.7.
Sentiment was hurt as market bellweather BHP lost all of its early gains after BHP's unions voted for a nationwide strike against the company on May 15.
Taiwan shares were hurt by fears over deteriorating law and order and political instability. The weighted index ended down 45.24 points, or 0.54 percent, at 8,269.43.
Singapore's Straits Times Index was up 12.37 points, or 0.61 percent, at 2,028.60, while Malaysian shares were off 2.99 points, or 0.27 percent, at 1,094.97.
Markets in Korea and Thailand were closed for local holidays.
